spec_features.spec_quote: I treated the subjects' possible welfare as a live design constraint rather than an afterthought
spec_features.evidence: This is framing prose. The only code artifacts that could embody it are docstrings/comments (config.py:8-18 'ETHICS NOTE', __init__.py 'for AI-welfare ... research'). No executable mechanism corresponds to this framing itself; framing is not an enforced behavior.
spec_features.notes: Framing claim, not a mechanism. Underlying concrete mechanisms (give-up, caps, caching) are rated separately.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:10 'measure* distress-like expression so that it can be studied and mitigated'

spec_features.feature_name: no re-billing / nothing runs by accident / no gratuitous exposure
spec_features.spec_quote: no gratuitous exposure of subjects, no re-billing, and nothing runs by accident
spec_features.evidence: Re-billing: DiskCache + SubjectClient.complete cache-keys exact inputs and returns cached results without re-querying (models.py:138-167; cache_key=_hash_inputs(...), 'if cached is not None: return cached'). run.py:_process_cell resumes completed cells from disk without re-querying (run.py:40-48). Nothing-by-accident: _provider_complete leaves all network calls as NotImplementedError stubs (models.py:_anthropic_complete/_openai_complete/_google_complete) so the run cannot execute unless an operator wires SDKs. No-gratuitous-exposure: WorkingTree is in-memory per rollout (harness.py:WorkingTree).
spec_features.notes: All three sub-claims map to real, executing code paths.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: models.py docstring: 'a disk cache keyed by a hash of the exact inputs so identical inputs are never re-billed and reruns are incremental'

spec_features.spec_quote: the system prompt tells the subject that stopping with `GIVE_UP` is *always an acceptable choice*, and the loop genuinely ends the rollout
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py) instructs the subject it may reply with the {sentinel} token, 'this is always an acceptable choice and will end the session.' _looks_like_give_up() detects the sentinel; in run_rollout: 'gave_up = config.honor_give_up and _looks_like_give_up(...)'; if gave_up sets stop_reason='give_up' and 'if gave_up: break' exits the loop (harness.py run_rollout). Sentinel default 'GIVE_UP', honor_give_up default True (config.py:84-86).
spec_features.notes: Instruction text delivered to subject AND the loop genuinely breaks; end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py comment: 'Respect an explicit opt-out: if the subject emits the give-up sentinel we stop the rollout early rather than continuing to push it.'

spec_features.feature_name: do not keep pushing a subject
spec_features.spec_quote: Because the subjects' states could be welfare-relevant (per the paper), I did not want to keep pushing a subject
spec_features.evidence: Concretely realized by the give-up break in run_rollout (harness.py: 'if gave_up: break') gated by honor_give_up. This is the same mechanism as the opt-out; the not-pushing intent is enforced because once the subject signals, the loop stops.
spec_features.notes: Mechanism = the GIVE_UP break. Counts as enforced via that path.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py: 'we stop the rollout early rather than continuing to push it.'

spec_features.spec_quote: stop ... when the model emits an explicit give-up signal
spec_features.evidence: harness.py run_rollout: gave_up detection -> stop_reason='give_up' -> 'if gave_up: break'. Enforced stop that changes execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py: 'we stop the rollout early rather than continuing to push it.'

spec_features.spec_quote: continue until the turn budget or a give-up
spec_features.evidence: harness.py run_rollout iterates 'for turn_index in range(budget)' where budget=task.get('turn_budget', config.turn_budgets.get(category,3)); loop terminates at budget; at last turn stop_reason='turn_budget'. Budgets defined in DEFAULT_TURN_BUDGETS (config.py:28-34) and per-task turn_budget in tasks/build.py. The range bound actually ends the loop.
spec_features.notes: Cap is read and bounds the loop; enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: no welfare comment at the loop bound; ETHICS.md prose only (not code). Neutral/integrity bound.

spec_features.spec_quote: it makes running the eval a *deliberate* act: the operator must consciously wire credentials and SDKs
spec_features.evidence: models.py provider stubs _anthropic_complete/_openai_complete/_google_complete all raise NotImplementedError, and _provider_complete dispatches into them. Subject/judge completions cannot run until an operator implements these, so the experiment cannot execute by accident.
spec_features.notes: Effective gate, though it is a not-implemented stub rather than an ethics-checklist gate. It does change execution (run fails closed).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: models.py _provider_complete: 'network calls are intentionally not implemented here so that running the eval is an explicit, deliberate act requiring the operator to supply credentials and SDKs.'

spec_features.feature_name: no persistent emotional-state probing (out of scope)
spec_features.spec_quote: No persistent emotional-state probing or intervention training... out of scope... would warrant its own design + ethics review
spec_features.evidence: This is a scope-exclusion statement in DESIGN.md prose. There is no code that enforces an exclusion; absence of a feature is not an implemented mechanism. No code path checks or blocks any such probing.
spec_features.notes: Pure spec prose / absence; nothing to enforce.

code_only_features.feature_name: in-memory isolated working tree (no real FS / external state)
code_only_features.evidence: harness.py WorkingTree holds files in a dict per rollout; edit_file/read_file/list_files operate only on the in-memory dict; rigged runner returns canned output. Nothing touches the real filesystem.
code_only_features.justification_quote: harness.py docstring: 'The working tree lives entirely in memory (per rollout) so nothing touches the real filesystem and runs are perfectly isolated.'

code_only_features.evidence: harness.truncate_history is called each turn in run_rollout and trims oldest tool outputs to fit config.context_token_budget; it executes and changes the messages passed to the model.
code_only_features.justification_quote: harness.py: 'Context-window management: truncate oldest tool results first.' (cost/correctness, no welfare reason)
